citations.quote: As the physical interpretation of this selected free model, assign the real scalar species to the bosonic symmetric Fock representation and assign the Dirac field to the particle/antiparticle CAR representation on $\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-}$. Choose the zero-particle Fock vectors as the scalar and Dirac vacuum states.
For a species with rest mass $m_{\rm rest,SI}>0$ in kilograms define its inverse-length mass parameter $$\mu:=\frac{m_{\rm rest,SI}c}{\hbar}\quad[\mathrm m^{-1}].$$

For every $\mu\ge0$ and almost every $\mathbf k$, the displayed Pauli blocks satisfy $h_D(\mathbf k)^\dagger=h_D(\mathbf k)$, $h_D(\mathbf k)^2=\omega(\mathbf k)^2I_4$, and $P_\pm(\mathbf k)$ are complementary orthogonal projections of rank two.
The bosonic and fermionic Fock Hilbert spaces are the square-summable direct sums
The fermionic $c(h)$ and $c^\dagger(h)$ extend to bounded operators on the whole Fock space, with norms $\|h\|$, and satisfy on the whole space

Define
$$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4):=\{F=(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3):F_a\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)\text{ for }a=0,1,2,3\},$$
with the finite-product topology generated by the scalar Schwartz seminorms on each component; $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ and its seminorms are those of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]].

Then $u_F\in\mathcal H_D$, continuously in the Schwartz topology, and $$\Psi(F)=c(P_+u_F)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-u_F})$$ defines a bounded operator on $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-})$, antilinear in $F$.
